title: The Magna Carta
passages: On 15 June 1215, King John of England met a group of angry BARONS in a green meadow called Runnymede, beside the River Thames, about 20 miles west of London. The barons were tired of heavy taxes and unfair punishments, and they wanted the king to promise that he, too, would follow the law. John's royal seal was pressed into wax on a long document written in Latin on PARCHMENT. It held about 63 short sections, called clauses, covering everything from fish traps on rivers to the rights of widows.

The peace did not last. Within about ten weeks, Pope Innocent III declared the charter ANNULLED, and war broke out. Yet new versions were issued in 1216, 1217 and 1225, and its ideas kept spreading. Only four copies from 1215 survive today: two in the British Library, one at Lincoln CATHEDRAL and one at Salisbury. A later copy from 1297 is kept in Parliament House in Canberra, Australia, more than 16,000 kilometres from Runnymede. More than 800 years on, people around the world still talk about its promise that free people should not be punished without a fair trial.
